Man Wai-sum retired from the media six months ago. With a background in marketing management, Kingston Koo is abruptly appointed as director. Deputy Director Cheung Ka-yin takes over Leung King-yan’s status but struggles to gain the respect of her colleagues. Wai-sum makes a strong comeback as the Queen of News, acquiring the online media platform founded by Lau Yim and challenges conventional mainstream media. 文慧心（佘诗曼饰）退隐新闻界半年，SNK生巨变。市场管理出身的古肇华（黄宗泽饰）空降总监一职，视新闻为赚钱工具；副总监张家妍（李施嬅饰）取代了梁景仁（马国明饰）的地位，纵握大权却难服众。慧心以“新闻女王”姿态强势回归，收购刘艳（王敏奕饰）创办的网媒公开平台，向传统主流媒体发起挑战。KOL唐芷瑶（陈晓华饰）利用自媒体，对慧心展开恶意狙击。

To enjoy freshness, you have to eat it in season!! On James’ Going Places, the two chefs suit up tightly and head into the fields with a scooter brigade of local aunties. Slow-grown lettuce is harvested and eaten on the spot—crisp, fresh, and straight from the field! Lukang’s shrimp monkeys are famously delicious, but the Shrimp Monkey King’s secret recipe is being revealed on camera for the very first time!

Canton Flavour S9 continues to present authentic Cantonese cuisines. By recording the farming and fishing of Guangdong farmers and fishermen on site, it stays close to the ground and spreads the positive energy of workers.

A petty official in the Tang Dynasty is given the impossible task of delivering fresh lychee from Lingnan to Imperial Consort Yang's birthday banquet in Chang'an, a distance of over 2500 kilometers. He has three months to make the impossible possible. The penalty for failure is death for him and slavery for his family.

Xiao Wu Xia, the young lord of Yueluo City, has been living in hiding in Liang Kingdom under the alias Wei Zhao, bearing the shame of being labeled a traitor. His mission is to uncover the truth behind his family’s downfall and capture the sole survivor of Prince Qi’s case. However, his plans are derailed by the unexpected arrival of Jiang Ci. Pei Yan takes the injured Jiang Ci into his home, aiming to discover who’s behind the disruption.

New Stirrings is an intimate, ground-up exploration of Singapore’s hawker culture told through the people who live and breathe it. From seasoned heritage hawkers who’ve spent decades perfecting their craft to next-generation hawkerpreneurs reshaping tradition with technology and creativity, the series journeys into the grit, flavour, and heart of the hawker culture. Episode 1 looks at the origins and fading legacy of Singapore’s hawker culture and the veteran hawkers whose perseverance have kept it alive. Episode 2 explores how hawkers reinvent themselves amid shifting tastes, revealing the evolving flavours of the trade. Lastly, episode 3 shows us a glimpse into the new generation of hawkers and technologies including robots that are reshaping hawker culture. More than a food series, New Stirrings is a celebration of the people behind the wok, reminding us that behind every dish is a story.

Modern women with new-age beliefs. Is marriage really hell or bliss? Papa Hao is a widowed restaurant chef who single-handedly raised three daughters. Eldest daughter Meiman is a successful advertising agent who believes that women should always place career before marriage. Ironic to her extravagant lifestyle, Meiman ends up with her miserly colleague whom she bickers with incessantly from workplace to home.. Second daughter Meili is a TV producer who yearns to start a family but is always rejected by her matchmaking prospects because of her ordinary looks. When she finally chances upon her Korean Prince Charming, she finds that her younger sister too has fallen for the same guy...Youngest daughter Meide is an independent and open-minded graduate who has been spoilt by her father and sisters. While she enjoys the pursuit by her suitors, she does not equate love to marriage. Not until she meets her traditional mother-in-law-to-be and sparks start flying... Like all romantic fairy tales, will the three sisters get married and live happily ever after?

The situation sparks a full-blown love war between the women. Shanxi, the cradle of Chinese civilization, has witnessed the integration and coexistence of diverse ethnic cultures. Taiyuan, the capital located in central Shanxi Province, is a microcosm of the region. Founded in 497 BCE, it has served as the capital of nine dynasties and has borne witness to more than 2,500 years of historical culture and change. The Fen River flows through the city, nurturing countless cultural treasures above the ground.

Keti and her son Nika find themselves in huge trouble when he hits an old man with his car. With the victim’s family threatening to press charges, Keti must find a way to raise a huge sum of money or Nika might go to prison.

Motherhood has not been easy for Asia, a single mother whose teenage daughter, Vika, barely interacts with her. But when Vika’s health deteriorates rapidly, Asia must step in and become the mother Vika so desperately needs.

Twice a year, Asia’s coastlines enter a brief, rare window of extraordinary equinox “king tides” where the Sun, Moon and Earth align and the sea surges beyond its usual limits. In that short period, homes, sea walls, livelihoods and ecosystems are stress-tested and the shoreline becomes a moving border. Tides of Time is a three-part series narrated by BAFTA-nominated presenter and Sunday Times best-selling author Ben Fogle. Filmed in Bangladesh, China and South Korea, the team chases this celestial trigger along three epic shores where water doesn’t just rise but rewrites the communities’ destinies. From Sundarbans’ Hanging Homes Village, to China’s Qiantang “Silver Dragon” tidal bore, to Korea’s getbol mudflats, each film is a human rendezvous with the tide where humans must choose to adapt, resist or surrender.
Spotlight on East Asia, a region steeped in history and now helping to write the future of our world. We'll break down the key stories and explain why they matter.

In an age where loneliness is common and connection feels like currency, a new kind of companion has arrived on the market: the AI chatbot. Always awake, always responsive, always affirming. But how much of a real friend or companion can something digital ever be? Our series follows four individuals here in Singapore – different in age, culture, circumstance, yet united by a willingness to explore something different. Over the course of two weeks, each participant shapes their own “ideal” AI companion and introduces it into their life. We witness the ups and downs of these encounters, examining and analysing emotional motivations and algorithmic responses with experts ranging from relationship coaches to AI developers. In the end, the question is: Can AI really fill that human space where a friend or a companion should be?
